$comment: Reviewed mapping of OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 levels 1-2 and MASVS 2.x to this repository. Edit statuses here, then run `pnpm security:checklist` to regenerate docs/security/checklist.md.

statuses.met: Implemented and verified in this repository.
statuses.partial: Partly implemented; the note says what is missing and when it lands.
statuses.deployment: Depends on production infrastructure set up in phase 12; the note says what the application already does.
statuses.accepted: A documented deviation with compensating controls (ADR-048).
statuses.not-applicable: The platform does not use the technology or feature.

V1.1.1.note: Express parses JSON, query strings and path parameters once; Zod validates the decoded values and nothing decodes them again afterwards.

V1.1.2.note: Encoding happens at the sink: React escapes text at render, Prisma passes parameters to the driver, email templates escape HTML as they render, nodemailer encodes headers.

V1.2.1.note: React escapes element text and attributes; the email templates escape every inserted value; response headers are set from validated values only.

V1.2.2.note: URLs are built with URL, URLSearchParams and encodeURIComponent. CMS links and trust-signal evidence must be https; return paths after sign-in must be same-site (safeNext).

V1.2.3.note: JSON comes from JSON.stringify; JSON-LD escapes `<` so it cannot close the script element. No script is assembled from strings.

V1.2.4.note: Prisma queries and tagged-template raw SQL are parameterised. The one use of unsafe raw SQL (key rotation) takes table and column names from the static ENCRYPTED_FIELDS registry and passes values as parameters.

V1.2.5.note: The applications never start operating system processes.

V1.2.9.note: Regular expressions are built only from constants. Search text reaches PostgreSQL trigram functions as a query parameter, never as a pattern.

V1.3.1.note: No WYSIWYG or HTML input: CMS content is structured plain text that React renders as text.

V1.3.2.note: No eval or new Function in application code. Production CSPs omit unsafe-eval, so the browser would refuse it anyway (development builds need it for React Refresh).

V1.3.3.note: Values bound for file names, storage keys, slugs and search are schema-checked for character set and length, and file names are reduced to a safe form.

V1.3.4.note: Users cannot upload SVG: documents are accepted only as PDF, JPEG or PNG by content. The only SVGs are QR codes drawn locally.

V1.3.5.note: No user-supplied Markdown, CSS, XSL or similar is rendered.

V1.3.6.note: Outbound hosts come from configuration or constants; no request makes the server fetch a URL it supplies. next/image loads only https images from IMAGE_REMOTE_HOSTS; trust-signal evidence URLs are stored, never fetched.

V1.3.7.note: Email and PDF templates are code; user values are inserted as escaped data, never as template source.

V1.3.9.note: No memcache. Redis keys are built from validated ids and HMAC digests, and values are JSON.

V1.3.10.note: Message formats come only from the typed catalog; user values are arguments, never formats.

V1.3.11.note: Recipient addresses pass Zod email validation; nodemailer encodes headers and rejects line breaks; subjects come from the catalog.

V1.4.1.note: The platform is written in TypeScript and runs on memory-safe JavaScript runtimes (Node.js, browsers, Hermes); no native code of ours handles input.

V1.4.2.note: Money is bigint minor units; numeric inputs are schema-bounded integers.

V1.4.3.note: The platform is written in TypeScript and runs on memory-safe JavaScript runtimes (Node.js, browsers, Hermes); no native code of ours handles input.

V1.5.2.note: Only JSON.parse followed by Zod parsing into plain objects; no class-based or native deserialization of untrusted data.

V2.1.1.note: Every route publishes its Zod input schemas in openapi.json (formats, lengths, enums, patterns). Shared schemas define emails, phones, airport codes, money and passengers.

V2.1.2.note: Cross-field rules live in shared code used by API and clients: document expiry after travel, infants per adult, legs in order, check-out after check-in, stay length.

V2.2.1.note: All input is validated against schemas with allowlisted values, patterns and ranges (level 2: all input).

V2.2.2.note: The API validates every request; client-side checks reuse the same rules for usability only.

V2.3.1.note: Bookings move only through the audited state machine; payment, ticketing and refunds check the current status.

V2.3.3.note: Status changes, ledger postings and audit entries are written in one database transaction.

V2.3.4.note: Seats are reserved with a conditional update inside the booking transaction (409 sold-out).

V3.2.1.note: The API sends CSP default-src 'none', nosniff and exact JSON content types. Files are served as attachments with nosniff and a sandbox CSP.

V3.2.2.note: React renders data as text; the only raw HTML is escaped JSON-LD and QR codes drawn locally.

V3.3.1.note: Session cookies are Secure with the __Secure- prefix; the website's own cookies use __Host- in production. Plain-HTTP development drops the prefixes.

V3.3.2.note: Access and CSRF cookies are SameSite=Lax, the refresh cookie Strict (and only sent to /v1/auth), preference and consent cookies Lax.

V3.3.3.note: The API's session cookies are designed to be shared between the web host and the API host (COOKIE_DOMAIN), so they use __Secure-. Every other cookie uses __Host-.

V3.3.4.note: Access and refresh cookies are HttpOnly and set only through Set-Cookie. The CSRF cookie is readable on purpose so the page can echo it.

V3.4.1.note: HSTS max-age two years with includeSubDomains and preload on API, web and console responses.

V3.4.2.note: CORS answers only origins in CORS_ORIGINS (required in production); admin origins must also be listed.

V3.4.3.note: Per-response nonce CSP with strict-dynamic, object-src 'none' and base-uri 'none' on web and console; default-src 'none' on the API.

V3.4.5.note: Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin everywhere; guest tokens travel in URL fragments, which are never sent.

V3.4.6.note: frame-ancestors 'none' on every response of the web, console and API.

V3.5.1.note: Cookie-authenticated unsafe requests need a session-bound CSRF token in X-CSRF-Token; admin calls also need an allowlisted Origin.

V3.5.2.note: Sensitive calls require X-CSRF-Token (not CORS-safelisted) and JSON bodies, so they always trigger a preflight.

V3.5.3.note: State changes use POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE; emailed links open pages that send the token with POST.

V3.5.4.note: Website, console and API are separate applications on separate hosts; production requires https admin origins. Final hostnames are set in phase 12.

V3.7.1.note: React, Next.js and React Native only; no plugins.

V3.7.2.note: Redirects go to same-site paths (safeNext) or to the checkout URL a configured payment provider returns from its API.

V4.1.1.note: JSON and problem+json responses carry charset=utf-8; Next.js pages declare UTF-8.

V4.1.2.note: Edge configuration (phase 12): redirect HTTP to HTTPS only on the web and console hosts; the API host answers HTTPS only. HSTS preload already covers all three.

V4.1.3.note: Client IPs come from X-Forwarded-For only through TRUST_PROXY_HOPS trusted hops; the country header is read only when configured for an edge that overwrites it. The edge settings are part of phase 12.

V4.2.1.note: Node's HTTP parser rejects messages with conflicting Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding; load balancer settings come with phase 12.

V5.1.1.note: Visa documents: PDF, JPEG or PNG by content, 10 MB, 60 per application, scanned before anyone can open them; infected files are deleted and the traveller is asked for another. No archives.

V5.2.1.note: Uploads are read with a size limit after the ownership check.

V5.2.2.note: The type is decided from the magic bytes; the stored name gets the extension of that type, so name and content always match. Anything else is refused.

V5.3.1.note: Uploads go to private object storage, never to a served folder, and are only returned as attachments.

V5.3.2.note: Storage keys are generated ids; user file names are only shown, after sanitising.

V5.4.1.note: Downloads set Content-Disposition attachment with a generated, sanitised file name.

V5.4.2.note: File names are reduced to letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore before use in headers.

V5.4.3.note: ClamAV scans every document; production refuses the mock scanner.

V6.2.4.note: 9,126 common passwords that meet the length rule.

V6.2.6.note: Password fields are masked (type=password, secureTextEntry), with a show toggle.

V6.2.7.note: No paste blocking; current-password and new-password autocomplete for password managers.

V6.2.8.note: Passwords are hashed exactly as typed: no trimming, truncation or case change.

V6.2.12.note: Have I Been Pwned range API (k-anonymity). If it does not answer within 2.5 s the check is skipped and logged.

V6.3.2.note: No default accounts. The optional seeded admin needs SEED_ADMIN_* and is refused in production.

V6.3.3.note: Staff must use MFA. For travellers MFA is offered but optional; compensating controls and the rationale are in ADR-048.

V6.3.4.note: Every pathway ends in completeSignIn(), which applies MFA and auditing the same way.

V6.4.1.note: No system-generated passwords. Verification and reset links are 256-bit, single use, 24 hours and 30 minutes.

V6.4.2.note: No password hints or security questions.

V6.4.3.note: Reset never signs the person in, ends every session, and MFA is still asked at the next sign-in.

V6.5.1.note: TOTP steps, recovery codes and texted codes are each usable once.

V6.5.2.note: Recovery codes (50 bits) are stored with argon2id.

V6.5.4.note: Texted codes: 6 digits. Recovery codes: 50 bits.

V6.5.5.note: Texted codes live 5 minutes. TOTP uses 30-second steps and accepts one step of clock drift (RFC 6238), each step once; see ADR-048.

V6.6.1.note: Texted codes go only to the number they prove; an authenticator is offered to every traveller, and phone sign-in and the profile explain the risk of texted codes.

V6.6.2.note: Codes are bound to their purpose and number; a new request replaces the old code.

V6.6.3.note: 5 attempts per code, 3 sends per number per 10 minutes, per-IP limits.

V6.8.1.note: Social identities are unique by provider and subject; linking needs a verified email.

V6.8.4.note: Provider sign-in counts as one factor; staff and step-up need our own TOTP.

V7.1.1.note: Includes the justification against NIST SP 800-63B for traveller sessions.

V7.2.4.note: Every sign-in, including MFA completion, issues new tokens. Re-authentication and step-up raise assurance on the current session without rotating it; see ADR-048.

V7.4.1.note: Revoked sessions go on a Redis denylist, so their access tokens fail at once.

V7.4.3.note: A password change ends the other sessions; reset ends all; the session list can sign out every other device.

V7.5.1.note: Phone changes and MFA enrolment need a fresh proof; disabling MFA or new recovery codes need a code; email cannot be changed.

V7.5.2.note: Signing out another device needs a fresh proof.

V7.6.2.note: Sessions start only from an explicit sign-in; there is no silent single sign-on.

V8.2.3.note: Responses are filtered through their schema; restricted fields are masked or never included.

V9.1.2.note: Access tokens: EdDSA only. Provider ID tokens: RS256 or ES256 only.

V9.1.3.note: Keys come from configuration or fixed provider JWKS URLs; jku, x5u and jwk headers are ignored.

V9.2.2.note: Access tokens carry typ at+jwt and are checked for it; ID tokens are accepted only by the social sign-in route.

V9.2.4.note: One signing key for one audience (the API).

V10.1.1.note: On the web, tokens live in HttpOnly cookies the page cannot read, and the refresh cookie only reaches /v1/auth. The app keeps the access token in memory and the refresh token in the Keychain or Keystore.

V10.1.2.note: Each provider sign-in uses a fresh single-use nonce issued by the API; the JSON-only endpoint behind the CORS allowlist cannot be called cross-site.

V10.2.1.note: No OAuth code flow: the web and the app get ID tokens from the providers' own SDKs with our nonce.

V10.2.2.note: The issuer is checked against the expected value for each provider.

V10.3.2.note: Decisions use sub, roles and the session id.

V10.3.3.note: Users are identified by sub (a UUID) from our own issuer.

V10.3.4.note: The mfa claim and the server-side step-up time gate staff and step-up routes.

V10.4.1.note: The platform is not an OAuth authorization server or OpenID provider. It issues its own session tokens and relies on Google and Apple only as identity providers.

V10.4.2.note: The platform is not an OAuth authorization server or OpenID provider. It issues its own session tokens and relies on Google and Apple only as identity providers.

V10.4.11.note: The platform is not an OAuth authorization server or OpenID provider. It issues its own session tokens and relies on Google and Apple only as identity providers.

V10.4.5.note: Applied to our own refresh tokens: rotation on every use, reuse ends the session.

V10.4.8.note: Applied to our own refresh tokens: 90 days absolute.

V10.4.9.note: Applied to our own sessions: travellers see and sign out devices; staff can sign out any account.

V10.5.3.note: No discovery metadata: issuers and JWKS URLs are fixed in code.

V10.5.4.note: The audience must be one of our configured client ids.

V10.6.1.note: The platform is not an OAuth authorization server or OpenID provider. It issues its own session tokens and relies on Google and Apple only as identity providers.

V10.7.3.note: The platform is not an OAuth authorization server or OpenID provider. It issues its own session tokens and relies on Google and Apple only as identity providers.

V11.1.1.note: Generation, custody, rotation, compromise and retirement, following the NIST SP 800-57 life-cycle phases.

V11.2.1.note: Node.js crypto (OpenSSL), jose and argon2; nothing hand-rolled.

V11.2.2.note: Ciphertexts carry a key id, tokens a kid, password hashes their parameters.

V11.3.3.note: GCM with the record-bound context as additional data.

V11.4.1.note: SHA-256 and SHA-512 for general use. SHA-1 appears only inside HMAC-SHA-1 for TOTP (RFC 6238) and in the Have I Been Pwned k-anonymity protocol, where it protects nothing. No MD5.

V11.4.2.note: argon2id, 19 MiB, 2 passes, rehash on sign-in when parameters rise.

V11.4.4.note: No keys are derived from passwords.

V11.5.1.note: Tokens and secrets are 256-bit from the CSPRNG. Voucher codes carry about 99 bits; see ADR-048.

V12.1.1.note: The edge TLS policy (TLS 1.2 and 1.3, 1.3 preferred) comes with phase 12. Node clients already refuse anything below TLS 1.2.

V12.1.2.note: Cipher suites are set with the edge TLS policy in phase 12.

V12.2.1.note: HSTS with preload is already on every response; the edge serves TLS only (phase 12).

V12.2.2.note: Publicly trusted certificates are issued at the edge in phase 12.

V12.3.1.note: The application refuses plaintext in production for providers, Postgres, Redis, the worker-to-API hop, OTLP and SMTP, except declared private paths. ClamAV has no TLS and must run on the same host or a private network (phase 12).

V12.3.2.note: No client disables certificate verification; production Postgres URLs require sslmode with verification.

V12.3.3.note: The worker must call the API over https in production. The web and console servers' API URLs are set to https in phase 12.

V12.3.4.note: Internal certificates and CA pinning for managed services are set up in phase 12.

V13.2.1.note: The worker authenticates to the internal API with a static bearer token over TLS, and the services use password credentials for Postgres and Redis. Phase 12 replaces these with workload identity and short-lived credentials.

V13.2.2.note: Separate least-privilege database roles for the application and migrations, and scoped cloud identities, come with phase 12.

V13.2.3.note: Production refuses the local development token; every secret is generated per environment.

V13.2.4.note: Application-level allowlist of hosts; an egress firewall follows in phase 12.

V13.3.1.note: Secrets live in the cloud secret manager (phase 12); the application reads them only from the environment.

V13.3.2.note: Per-service access to secrets is set up with the secret manager in phase 12.

V13.4.1.note: Container images are built without source control metadata in phase 12.

V13.4.2.note: Production builds only. Production refuses mock providers, the demo seed and the seeded admin, and responses never contain stack traces.

V13.4.3.note: The API serves no static files; Next.js serves only public assets, without listings.

V13.4.4.note: The API answers TRACE with 404 (checked 2026-10-12). The edge blocks TRACE on every host in phase 12.

V13.4.5.note: No API documentation UI in any environment; the worker's health port is internal; metrics are pushed over OTLP, not exposed.

V14.2.1.note: Tokens travel in headers, bodies or URL fragments. The exception is signed document links, whose query carries a 5-minute signature for one document; see ADR-048.

V14.2.2.note: API responses are Cache-Control no-store; the website caches only public reads.

V14.2.3.note: No third-party trackers; error reports are scrubbed; optional categories need consent.

V14.3.1.note: Sign-out clears tokens, booking tokens and cached personal data on the web and in the app.

V14.3.2.note: Cache-Control no-store on every API response; private pages render their data client-side from the API.

V14.3.3.note: Browser storage holds preferences, recent searches, guest booking tokens (session-scoped) and, for one tab, a surname typed for the add-on lookup.

V15.1.2.note: CycloneDX SBOM on every security run; packages come only from the npm registry with a frozen lockfile.

V15.2.1.note: CI fails on high or critical advisories; exceptions are reviewed monthly.

V15.2.3.note: Production refuses mock adapters, the demo seed and development tokens; test code is not part of the builds.

V15.3.2.note: Every outbound HTTP client uses redirect: error.

V15.3.3.note: Zod drops fields that a body schema does not list.

V15.3.4.note: TRUST_PROXY_HOPS decides how much of X-Forwarded-For to trust; the edge is configured to overwrite it in phase 12.

V15.3.5.note: TypeScript strict mode, eqeqeq, and schema-typed inputs.

V15.3.6.note: Inputs become new objects through Zod; lookups use Map and Set; no deep merges of user input.

V15.3.7.note: Body, query and path each have their own schema; repeated parameters fail validation.

V16.2.1.note: Timestamp, request id, route, actor and target on log lines and audit entries.

V16.2.2.note: UTC timestamps everywhere; host clocks are kept in sync by the managed runtime.

V16.2.4.note: JSON lines with a request id shared across services.

V16.3.3.note: Validation failures, rate limits and bot-check failures are logged; 403 and 429 at warn.

V16.4.2.note: The audit log is append-only in the database. Access to the log service is configured in phase 12.

V16.4.3.note: Logs leave each container on stdout; shipping to a separate log service is part of phase 12.

V16.5.3.note: Errors roll transactions back; credential checks fail closed. Only the request rate limiter fails open, by documented choice.

V17.1.1.note: No WebRTC, TURN, media or signalling servers.

V17.2.1.note: No WebRTC, TURN, media or signalling servers.

V17.2.2.note: No WebRTC, TURN, media or signalling servers.

V17.3.1.note: No WebRTC, TURN, media or signalling servers.

V17.3.2.note: No WebRTC, TURN, media or signalling servers.

MASVS-STORAGE-1.note: Tokens and keys in the Keychain or Keystore (this device only); personal data offline in AES-256 MMKV; never AsyncStorage.

MASVS-STORAGE-2.note: Backups disabled, screen capture blocked on sensitive screens, scrubbed error reports, exports deleted after sharing, and a secret scan of the bundle.

MASVS-CRYPTO-1.note: Platform keystores and MMKV AES-256; keys from the platform CSPRNG.

MASVS-CRYPTO-2.note: The cache key is generated on the device, kept in the keystore and replaced on sign-out and account deletion.

MASVS-AUTH-1.note: Short-lived bearer token in memory, refresh token in the keystore, single-flight refresh; the server decides everything.

MASVS-AUTH-2.note: No local (biometric or device credential) authentication.

MASVS-AUTH-3.note: Export, deletion, phone changes and signing out other devices need a fresh proof.

MASVS-NETWORK-1.note: HTTPS only; cleartext is allowed only in development variants.

MASVS-PLATFORM-1.note: Incoming URLs pass an allowlist; app links are verified; guest tokens never reach the router.

MASVS-PLATFORM-2.note: No WebViews: hosted checkout opens in the system browser session.

MASVS-PLATFORM-3.note: Sensitive screens block capture and hide in the app switcher; secret fields are masked.

MASVS-CODE-1.note: Targets Android API 36; supports Android 7.0 and iOS 15.1 and later for reach in the primary market; see ADR-048.

MASVS-CODE-2.note: MOBILE_MIN_VERSION blocks builds below a version and the app asks for the update.

MASVS-CODE-4.note: Shared schemas validate input on the device; the API validates again.

MASVS-RESILIENCE-1.note: App Attest and Play Integrity are wired with report and strict modes; real verifiers need the owner's Apple and Google accounts (open owner question).

MASVS-RESILIENCE-2.note: No anti-tampering beyond attestation; see ADR-048.

MASVS-RESILIENCE-3.note: No obfuscation beyond Hermes bytecode; the bundle holds no secrets (scanned); see ADR-048.

MASVS-PRIVACY-1.note: Push permission only after a booking or from Account; documents (visa, licence, driver) only through the system picker; the camera only on the operator scan screen, for bus operator agents, as a barcode scanner without microphone; no location, contacts or photos access.

MASVS-PRIVACY-2.note: No advertising ids or trackers; error reports carry no personal data.

MASVS-PRIVACY-3.note: The privacy policy text and the store privacy labels come from the owner (open owner question).

MASVS-PRIVACY-4.note: Data export and account deletion in the app; notification preferences per channel.
